It is made from 100% WHEAT flour, and it is permitted to keep the word そば only by a specific exemption negotiated with Japan’s fair-trade authorities — every other noodle sold as そば must contain at least 30% buckwheat. So a coeliac who has learned to be wary of soba for the usual reason (二八, 打ち粉, shared water) will still be wrong here, and wrong in the opposite direction: this is not soba with some wheat in it, it is a wheat noodle wearing the name. It appears twice on this menu, as a bowl and as ゴーヤめし’s companion. ⚠ THE SECOND TRAP IS 麸 AND IT RUNS THE OTHER WAY. フーチャンプルー is built on 麸 — FU, which is pure WHEAT GLUTEN, the most concentrated wheat product in Japanese cooking — and yet fu is entirely plant-based, so a vegan scanning for a tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry may land on precisely the dish a coeliac must avoid most. The two diets fail on opposite halves of this menu repeatedly. ⚠ AND ソーミンチャンプルー IS SOMEN: wheat noodles, stir-fried. This is a NIIGATA regional restaurant — hegi soba, Tochio abura-age, tare-katsu, Sado mozuku, and nine local sakes on the drink-inclusive courses. ⚠ HEGI SOBA IS THE MOST INTERESTING SOBA CASE IN THIS DATASET AND IT IS STILL NOT A YES. tokyo_choi_baru_bocado.price_note: Full food and drink menus with prices, read from the shop’s own official page and the Gnavi menu pages it links. A COVER CHARGE of ¥450 (お通し代) applies per person, which the menu states outright. The course page gives a range of ¥4,800–6,800 and lists course components without individual prices; two are recorded below as named without price. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. ⚠ THE FORMAT IS THE STORY HERE. A Spanish-style bar built on tiny plates — ワンスプーン at ¥250–550, ワンフォークパスタ at ¥350, pinchos at ¥350–450 — is unusually workable for a restricted diet, because nothing is combined into a single main course that has to be rebuilt. A coeliac can order round the wheat rather than negotiating with it, and the cheapest safe things here cost ¥250. ⚠ BUT THE WHEAT IS SPREAD ACROSS FOUR WHOLE SECTIONS AND IT IS OBVIOUS IN THREE OF THEM. ワンフォークパスタ is pasta, all four of them. ミニクロワッサン is a croissant — the section name is the ingredient. ラップサラダ is a WRAP, which means a tortilla. And the pinchos section hides two: an アランチーニ and a カニクリームコロッケ are both crumbed, and フィッシュ&チップス is battered. ⚠ THE ONE THING WORTH KNOWING ABOUT PINCHOS THAT THIS MENU DOES NOT SAY: in Spain a pincho is conventionally served ON A SLICE OF BREAD, skewered through. Not one description here mentions bread, and several of these — the anchovy and cream cheese, the octopus and sardine, the liver pâté — are exactly the items that traditionally arrive on it. That is the question to ask of this section, and the menu will not answer it. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN THE MENU IS NEARLY CLOSED: 3種のローストきのこの旨味ピンチョス at ¥450 is the only dish with nothing animal named in it, and even that would conventionally sit on bread or under cheese. ⚠ AND THREE DRINKS ARE BEER IN DISGUISE: シャンディガフ, レモンビア and ピーチビア are all built on beer, so they are BARLEY — sold in the ビール section at ¥680 alongside fruit-flavoured names that read like cocktails.

tokyo_new_yorker_s_cafe_suidob.price_note: ⚠ NO ITEMS, AND THE NEAR-MISS HERE IS PARTICULARLY FRUSTRATING BECAUSE THE RIGHT DOCUMENT EXISTS. NEW YORKER’S Cafe is a Ginza Renoir chain, and its menu page links a file called カロリー・アレルギー物質情報 — calorie and ALLERGEN information — at menu/allergen.pdf. That is precisely the document this dataset most wants from any chain. It was downloaded: 1.8MB, and it extracts ONE CHARACTER. It is a pure image scan with no text layer whatsoever, so not a single dish name, calorie figure or allergen mark can be read from it. The menu page itself is the same story from the other direction — seven menu images with no useful alt text, nothing in the page text, and no HTML menu anywhere on the site. So the chain publishes both a menu and an allergen table, and neither is machine-readable. Tabelog is UNVERIFIED rather than empty: as of 2026-09-04 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ WHY THIS PATTERN KEEPS RECURRING AND IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN JUST NOTING: this is now the third chain in this dataset — with RAKERU and 俺の割烹 — that publishes allergen or menu data in a form no reader can use. RAKERU’s allergen table extracted but its dish names did not; 俺の割烹’s menu kept its English and lost its Japanese and every price; this one is a flat image. A published allergen chart that cannot be read is worth no more to a coeliac standing at the counter than no chart at all, and the failure is not the restaurant refusing to disclose — it is disclosure in a format that defeats the person who needs it. ⚠ NOTHING ABOUT WHAT THIS BRANCH SERVES IS RECORDED, deliberately. The menu-page thumbnails are captioned only as seasonal drinks, pasta and cakes, and inferring a pasta dish from a thumbnail label would be exactly the kind of guess this dataset forbids. A coffee-shop chain’s two standing questions — whether black coffee is on the board and whether any plant milk is offered — cannot be answered from an image. Re-check if Renoir ever republishes the allergen PDF with a text layer, or when Tabelog access returns.
